meta.title: Arion: voice input that stays on your computer
meta.description: Dictate into any app on macOS or Windows. Arion recognizes Chinese, English and both mixed on your device, works offline, and is open source under AGPL-3.0.
meta.ogAlt: The Arion icon over a soft, motion-blurred photograph of flowers

hero.title: Voice input that never leaves your computer
hero.lead: Press {shortcut} in any app and speak Chinese, English or both. Arion recognizes your speech on the device and types the text where your cursor is.
hero.note: Free and open source ({license}) · macOS {macos} or later · Windows preview
hero.demoLabel: Illustration: Arion listening in a dark pill below a document window, then typing the dictated sentence into the document.

editorLines: Onboarding now asks for one permission at a time.
The menu bar panel shows the last dictation.
demo.sentence: Before we merge this PR into main, let's run CI.

tour.title: Built for the way you talk at work

offline.title: Works offline
offline.body: Speech recognition runs on your device. After the one-time model download, dictation needs no network, and no audio or text is sent anywhere.
offline.mockLabel: Illustration: the menu bar shows the network off, and Arion's panel still receives a dictation recognized on the Mac.
offline.empty: Your dictations appear here until you quit.
offline.sentence: Move the design review to Thursday and send Lena the new build.

mixed.title: Two languages in one sentence
mixed.body: Switch between Chinese and English mid-sentence, the way people talk about code and meetings. You never pick a language first. While you speak, the text stays a draft in the pill; only the finished sentence is typed.
mixed.mockLabel: Illustration: a chat composer. Arion's pill shows the mixed Chinese and English draft revising as it streams, then the finished sentence is typed into the message box.
mixed.author: Lena
partials: hotfix 先合进 main，等 CI 过了
mixed.sentence: hotfix 先合进 main，等 CI 过了就发 beta。

learning.title: Learns from your fixes
learning.body: Correct a word Arion typed and it applies the fix next time, with an undo. Learned words stay on the device, encrypted.
learning.mockLabel: Illustration: a document where Arion typed “Orion”. The word is corrected to “Arion”, and the pill reports it as learned, with an undo.
learning.sentence: Sync with the {term} team on the roadmap tomorrow.

polish.title: Optional polishing
polish.body: A local language model (or a cloud model you connect) can tidy wording and apply spoken self-corrections before the text lands. Off by default.
polish.mockLabel: Illustration: the words as spoken, with fillers and a correction mid-sentence, above the tidy sentence Arion typed.
polish.spoken: um, so let's meet on Wednesday, no wait, Thursday at three
polish.polished: Let's meet on Thursday at three.

keyboard.title: A Pinyin keyboard in the same input method
keyboard.body: Arion's input method also types full Pinyin offline, with candidates that learn from the words you pick. Tap Shift to switch between Chinese and English; the badge by the cursor flips over to show which one is on.
keyboard.mockLabel: Illustration: typing “nihao” opens the candidate bar, the first candidate types 你好, then tapping Shift flips the badge by the cursor from 中 to A.

openSource.title: Build it with us
openSource.lead: Arion is open source under {license}. Fork the repository, fix what bothers you or build the feature you want, and open a pull request. Bug reports and ideas in Issues count too.
openSource.buildNote: Desktop builds need macOS, Go 1.27 and pnpm 10.

privacyPage.title: Privacy and encryption
privacyPage.lead: What Arion keeps, where, and what an account can and cannot do.

sections.title: What stays on your device
body: Microphone audio is held in memory for the dictation in progress and dropped when it ends. Drafts and corrections are kept the same way.

When you turn on context for polishing, Arion reads a bounded excerpt around the cursor in the focused field and visible text in the focused window through Accessibility. Nothing is stored, and password and unknown fields are skipped.
Usage statistics are daily totals of sessions, speaking time and words. They hold no text, app names or times of day.

sections.title: What uses the network
body: Model downloads: public files, each checked against a pinned SHA-256 digest before use.

Update checks: the release manifest from the Arion update center, carrying no content or device identifier. Updates verify a trusted signature before installing, and automatic checks can be turned off.

Optional sign-in and cloud polishing: the account service is contacted only when you sign in or manage your account; if you connect a cloud polishing provider, only the recognized text and enabled context are sent, never audio. Arion has no cloud speech recognition. Optional account-linked daily usage reporting is described on the usage data page.

sections.title: Encryption on the device
body: Approved and learned vocabulary is sealed with AES-256-GCM. The key is generated on the device and kept in the login Keychain (this device only) on macOS, or with DPAPI on Windows.
A missing key or a failed integrity check is an error. Arion never falls back to plaintext.

sections.title: Sync
body: Sync is in development and not yet available. Its design is fixed in the specification: each record is encrypted on the device before upload, and only devices that hold the group key can read it.
A new device joins through one of your existing devices or your recovery key. Removing a device rotates the key for future writes.

The relay, hosted or self-hosted, can see timing, IP addresses, device and group routing identifiers and ciphertext sizes. Encryption does not hide that metadata, and it cannot protect a device that is already compromised.

sections.title: Your AstraFoundry account
body: An account is optional. Dictation, vocabulary and learning work without one.

Signing in tells the hosted relay who you are and whether you have access to hosted sync. The account holds no keys and cannot decrypt anything you sync, and neither can AstraFoundry. The hosted relay does know which account each sync space belongs to.
Signing out keeps your local keys and vocabulary. Turning sync off and deleting data from the server are separate actions.

sections.title: What cannot be undone
body: If you lose every device and your recovery key, synced data is gone. Account recovery restores sign-in, not data.
Text already downloaded to a device cannot be erased from it remotely, even after that device is removed.

selfHostingPage.title: Self-hosting the sync relay
selfHostingPage.lead: Run the relay on your own hardware, so even the ciphertext stays with you.
selfHostingPage.status: The relay is in development and has no release yet. This page describes its design so you can plan ahead.

sections.title: What the relay does
body: The relay stores authenticated, encrypted records and the revisions that order them, and hands them to your other devices. It never processes speech and never sees plaintext.
Devices push batches of encrypted changes, pull with an opaque cursor, and are enrolled or revoked through the relay.

sections.title: One core, two account modes
body: The same core runs hosted and self-hosted. It knows devices, envelopes, revisions and cursors, not accounts. An account gate in front of it has two modes.
noop, the default for self-hosting: there are no accounts. Every request is authenticated by the signature of an enrolled device.

oidc: the relay also requires a bearer token from an OpenID Connect issuer, checks its issuer, audience, expiry and sync entitlement, and maps the token's issuer and subject to a tenant. Device signatures are still required. AstraFoundry's hosted relay runs in this mode, and you can point it at your own identity provider.

sections.title: What you see as an operator
body: Timing, IP addresses, device and group routing identifiers and ciphertext sizes. Not content: backups of the relay database hold ciphertext only.

sections.title: Running it
body: The relay is a Go service with its own PostgreSQL database. Its container image, configuration reference and runbook ship with the first release.

selfHostingPage.source: Follow the relay in the repository
selfHostingPage.hostedBody: AstraFoundry will run the same relay as a hosted service.

sections.title: Your account
body: Signing in is optional. After model provisioning, local dictation, vocabulary and learning work without an account. Keep your sign-in credentials secure and use only an account you are authorized to access. Signing out removes the stored sign-in credential without deleting your local vocabulary or encryption keys.

sections.title: Privacy and connected services
body: Speech recognition runs on your device. Cloud polishing is optional and sends recognized text and enabled context to your chosen provider, never microphone audio. The provider’s own terms apply to that service. Read the Privacy Policy for details about local storage, account services and network activity.

sections.title: Hosted sync
body: Signing in does not by itself enable memory sync or grant access to a hosted service. Hosted sync requires availability, account entitlement and device setup. Any additional service terms must be presented before that service is enabled.

sections.title: Review your output
body: Speech recognition and polishing can make mistakes. Review the text before sending or relying on it. You remain responsible for the content you choose to share.

usageDataPage.title: Usage data and product improvement
usageDataPage.lead: An optional way to help improve Arion. Sharing starts only after you choose it and the account service confirms your consent.

sections.title: What is sent
body: Reports contain seven fields: productSlug (arion), sourceId (a random identifier scoped to your account and this installation), date (the calendar day), visited (whether Arion was used that day), sessions (completed dictations), speechMs (microphone time in milliseconds), and words (word count).

Reports use your signed-in account for authentication. AstraFoundry can associate these daily totals with your account and installation and observe the request IP address and arrival time. They are not anonymous.

sections.title: What is excluded
body: No microphone audio, dictated or typed text, keyboard input, vocabulary, clipboard contents, prompts, cursor or screen context, scene names, application identities, window titles or URLs are included. Reports contain no per-session timestamps.
This choice does not authorize cloud polishing, encrypted memory sync or diagnostic-log uploads. Those are separate workflows.

sections.title: When sharing starts and stops
body: The product improvement checkbox is off by default. Accepting the terms or signing in alone does not grant usage consent. Only activity collected while signed in with confirmed consent is eligible; earlier local history and signed-out activity are not uploaded.

You can turn sharing off in Settings → Account. Signing out stops reporting, and the server checks current consent for every write. Pending daily reports remain locally for at most 31 days and hold no authentication tokens. Turning sharing off does not delete reports already received by the service.
Local usage totals remain available in Overview even when sharing is off.
